title: NASA: LOST MISSIONS
subtitle: Spirit RPG Mission

story_arc.opening: Spirit was sent to Gusev Crater to investigate rocks and soils that might record ancient water.
story_arc.turn: A wheel became stuck, but the rover kept working as a stationary science platform near Home Plate.
story_arc.ending: As Martian winter approached, available solar energy fell. Spirit's last communication was received on March 22, 2010; NASA ended recovery efforts on May 25, 2011.
story_arc.emotional_line: Spirit could no longer drive, but it kept listening to Mars until it could no longer call home.

hardware.name: Spirit (MER-A)
hardware.what_it_was: A solar-powered robotic geologist about the size of a golf cart.
hardware.why_sent: To study rocks and soil in Gusev Crater for clues about water and whether ancient Mars could have been habitable.
hardware.instrument: Rock Abrasion Tool (RAT) and Alpha Particle X-ray Spectrometer (APXS)
hardware.discovery: Spirit found silica-rich soil near Home Plate, evidence of an environment shaped by water or steam.
hardware.why_left: A wheel became stuck in 2009. Spirit continued as a stationary science platform before losing contact during the Martian winter.
hardware.what_remains: The rover remains at its final location in Gusev Crater, along with its instruments and power system.

current_status.last_event: Last communication: March 22, 2010. NASA ended recovery efforts and completed the mission: May 25, 2011.

controls_tip: Move: arrows / WASD · Interact: A, Z, E, Enter or Space

gallery.title: Gusev from Spirit's eyes
gallery.kid_text: This is real Mars terrain seen by Spirit. The rover was not just driving: it was looking for clues in rocks and soil.

gallery.title: Spirit's self-portrait
gallery.kid_text: Spirit used its camera to build a big panorama. It helps us imagine where the rover worked.

gallery.title: A wheel uncovers a clue
gallery.kid_text: Spirit’s stuck wheel scratched the ground and exposed bright, nearly pure silica. Scientists linked it to water and possible hot springs or steam vents long ago.

gallery.title: Spirit’s landing site from orbit
gallery.kid_text: A camera on the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter could see the rover’s landing area from space, including tracks and nearby landmarks.

sample_facts.text: RAT polished rock surfaces so instruments could examine fresh material underneath.
Mini-TES identified minerals from a distance using infrared measurements.
APXS measured the chemical composition of rocks and soil.

dialogue.intro_npc_1: Welcome, R.O.M. Your scanner is online. This mission starts by observing a machine that stayed behind.
dialogue.intro_npc_2: Find Spirit, study the science tools, and rebuild the story from evidence instead of guesses.
dialogue.npc_hint: Look for tools, bright samples, and strange soil. Every object can unlock a part of the story.
dialogue.npc_first_hint: Spirit is north of here. Walk next to it and press A.
dialogue.rover_before_npc: A quiet rover rests in the dust. Maybe Dr. Vega can help you understand it.
dialogue.rover_intro: Spirit (MER-A) launched on June 10, 2003 and landed in Gusev Crater in January 2004.
dialogue.rover_after_id: Correct. Spirit lasted far longer than its planned 90-sol mission.
dialogue.rover_waiting: Spirit is still quiet. You need more clues: tools, samples, and an environmental challenge.
dialogue.case_locked: An orange tool case. First identify the rover so you know what the tools are for.
dialogue.case_open: You found the APXS kit. New skill unlocked: Chemical Analysis.
dialogue.case_fact: The MER archive in PDS includes APXS, Mossbauer, Microscopic Imager, RAT, Mini-TES, Navcam, Pancam, and more mission data.
dialogue.dish: Link antenna: a mission is not only a rover. It is also the network that receives and protects its data.
dialogue.soil_locked: Bright soil. You need a science tool before analyzing it.
dialogue.soil_done: You already recorded this bright soil.
dialogue.soil_fact: Spirit found silica-rich soil near Home Plate. NASA describes it as evidence of an environment shaped by water or steam in Mars' past.
dialogue.soil_good: Good. In the game, that science clue becomes part of the mystery.
dialogue.nothing: Nothing to inspect here. Try people, machines, tools, samples, or bright soil.

mission_length.prompt: Spirit's primary mission was planned to last:

options: Hot water or steam in the past
It got stuck, became a stationary science platform, and could not regain contact as winter reduced available energy
NASA turned it off to launch another rover

final_clues.text: SIMULATION CLUE: Solar power was dropping as the Martian winter came closer. This recreates the engineering problem; it does not change Spirit's historical ending.
CLUE #02: NASA reformulated Spirit as a stationary science platform after attempts to move it failed.
CLUE #03: Spirit did not communicate after March 22, 2010; final contact attempts ended May 25, 2011.

storm.start: Dust event! The sky turns orange and the rover's solar energy drops.
storm.fact: NASA reported Spirit stopped communicating as Martian winter approached and solar energy declined.
storm.success: SIMULATION COMPLETE: You protected the power budget. In the historical record, Spirit still lost contact as winter approached.

ending.title: You discovered the story of Spirit.
ending.tagline: They were left behind. Their stories weren't.
ending.codex_text: Spirit complete: planned for 90 sols, operated for more than six years, became a stationary science platform after getting stuck, and helped reveal watery, possibly hydrothermal environments on Mars.
